validity.researcher_notes: The pipeline is real. The Azerbaijan sources describe the Hajigabul to Mozdok line of 680 km, while the row is the Mozdok to Kazimagomed line. Whether the 680 km and 10 bcm figures fit this row should be confirmed by a person. No cited page names an operator or owner.

fills.researcher_notes: The Azerbaijan Ministry of Energy page (Oct 2025) says the Hajigabul to Mozdok pipeline has an annual capacity of 10 bcm. The 2023 IEA Azerbaijan energy profile says the same. Both describe the line from Azerbaijan to Mozdok, so the match to the Mozdok to Kazimagomed row rests on the shared name Mozdok. Wikipedia gives an original capacity of 13 bcm per year and an operating figure near 5 bcm, which the sheet does not use.

The Azerbaijan Ministry of Energy page (Oct 2025) says the pipeline is 680 km long, 200 km of it in Azerbaijan. Wikipedia gives the same 680 km. The ministry page describes the line from Hajigabul in Azerbaijan to Mozdok, so whether 680 km covers only the Russian Mozdok to Kazimagomed section is not settled.
Wikipedia gives a pipe diameter of 1,220 mm. A 2009 Vestnik Kavkaza item says the Baku to Novo-Filya line near the Russian border is 1220 mm. The second page covers the Azerbaijan leg only.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Newest dated reports are from January 2010 and show gas flowing to Dagestan. The Azerbaijan ministry says its exports through the line ended after 2014. No cited source states the current status.
